strengths: Well-motivated problem: Clearly identifies gap in existing metrics—insensitivity to geometric failures (FVD) vs. fragility to valid motion (VBench/MEt3R)
Comprehensive experimental scope: 1,296 videos across T2V/I2V/V2V paradigms with diverse real-world anchors; extensive controlled perturbations demonstrating monotonic SGC sensitivity
Physically grounded approach: Core principle (static background must obey single camera transformation) is intuitive and theoretically justified
Robustness analysis: Motion-stratified analysis effectively demonstrates SGC independence from camera dynamics; weak correlations with estimated camera motion on real data
Thorough ablations and validation: Tab. 2 ablations, component-specific perturbations (Fig. 7b), and 10-fold CV of PCA weights show methodological rigor
Clear presentation: Well-written with informative visualizations and detailed appendices including algorithms and hyperparameters
weaknesses: Critical dependence on unvalidated component estimators: SGC chains VGGT, Video Depth Anything, DELTA, and SegAnyMo without domain-specific validation on generated videos. No systematic sensitivity analysis for depth/pose/tracking errors. Cascading failures not quantified—metric may measure estimator consistency rather than true geometric coherence

Absence of human validation: No perceptual studies linking SGC optimization to perceived quality. No ground truth comparison against videos with known/injected geometric errors. Claims of 'effectively identifying critical failures' remain unsubstantiated

Limited technical novelty: Approach concatenates existing methods (VGGT→depth→tracking→MOS→PnP); depth clustering uses simplistic 1D k-means; PCA weighting is standard. High redundancy between local/global translational variance (r≈0.992) suggests over-parameterization. Core contribution reduces to method combination + standard aggregation

Methodological issues in baseline comparisons: MEt3R(+MOS) is non-standard formulation; VBench reweighted via PCA diverges from published methodology; selective masking of baselines introduces confounds. Comparisons lack external validation

PCA weight generalization concerns: Weights learned on full dataset and applied to same dataset (data leakage despite 10-fold CV). Future generative models may exhibit different failure distributions, invalidating learned weights. No analysis of weight stability under distribution shift

Limited scope and realism: Assumes rigid static backgrounds (water/vegetation legitimate deform); short clips (1-4s) insufficient for detecting temporal drift; approach only handles scenes with clear foreground-background separation

Missing ground truth validation: No oracle study with artificially injected/validated geometric errors. No comparison to reconstructed-from-real-3D videos (ground truth geometry). Real videos as 'anchors' weak—inherently have good geometry but insufficient to validate against controlled errors

Hyperparameter selection unexplained: kseg=10, Smin=200 appear arbitrary; no sensitivity study. PnP threshold selection and convergence rates not discussed. Generalization to different video lengths/content unclear
Incomplete reproducibility: No code release mentioned; track filtering thresholds and degenerate PnP handling underspecified. Hyperparameter optimization process not documented

Failure case analysis insufficient: When does SGC fail despite correct geometry? False positive/negative rates unknown. How do generated artifacts (noise, unrealistic motion, texture discontinuities) affect tracking/depth? Limited discussion of when metrics fail

strengths: Identifies and addresses a genuine gap in video generation evaluation: existing fidelity metrics are insensitive to geometric distortions while consistency metrics penalize valid foreground motion
Physically grounded principle (local pose variance as geometric consistency proxy) with clear interpretation

Exceptionally comprehensive experimental validation: synthetic perturbations demonstrate monotonic responsiveness, 10-fold CV confirms PCA weight stability (ρ=0.9989), component-specific perturbations validate individual metrics
Explicitly disentangles foreground dynamics from background stability through motion segmentation, addressing 'fragility-to-motion' bias that confounds existing consistency metrics
Thorough ablation studies including module-level analysis (Table 2), component correlations with principled justification (Fig. 7a), and sensitivity to MOS corruption (Fig. 8)
Strong practical utility: identifies geometric failures in Latte/Modelscope (high SGC scores) that score well on FVD/VBench-BC, demonstrating genuine complementarity
Exceptional reproducibility with detailed algorithms, hyperparameter specifications, implementation details, and code-ready descriptions enabling verification and adoption
Excellent presentation with clear writing, informative visualizations (Figs. 2-4), and intuitive mathematical exposition
weaknesses: Heavy dependency on recent sub-component models (VGGT, Video Depth Anything, DELTA, SegAnyMo, all 2024-2025) with unquantified error propagation; MOS sensitivity analysis shows >100% error increase under severe under-segmentation in dynamic scenes, but depth/pose estimation robustness not systematically analyzed
Absence of human perceptual evaluation studies: no validation that SGC-detected geometric failures correspond to visually noticeable problems; qualitative examples are illustrative but ungrounded

Ad-hoc aggregation design: PCA weighting is pragmatic but lacks theoretical justification; double normalization (Z-score + min-max) not well motivated; high correlation between local/global translational variance (r≈0.992) justified as hierarchical check but redundancy insufficiently explained

Limited generalization analysis: dataset spans resolutions and lengths with minimal discussion of sensitivity; PCA weights learned on specific distribution—out-of-distribution generalization to very different video domains unclear
No per-region or temporal diagnostic output: metric aggregates to single score without spatial/temporal decomposition, limiting practitioner insights into failure sources
Incomplete edge-case coverage: static-camera scenarios partially addressed but not systematic; textureless regions and high-depth-variation scenes not discussed
Baseline comparisons use custom adaptations: MEt3R(+MOS) is unpublished variant; VBench requires non-standard PCA aggregation, complicating future reproduction

Computational cost not analyzed: multiple DNNs required (VGGT, Video Depth Anything, DELTA, SegAnyMo) make deployment expensive relative to FVD/VBench, but no timing provided; 1D depth clustering strategy not compared against alternatives

strengths: Addresses a genuine and important gap in video generation evaluation: existing fidelity-centric metrics (FVD) miss geometric failures while consistency metrics penalize valid foreground motion. The problem formulation is clear and well-motivated.
Physically principled and elegant approach: constraining static backgrounds to a single rigid camera transformation is theoretically sound and avoids the 'fragility-to-motion' bias of prior work.

Exceptionally thorough experimental validation: 1,296 videos across 10 models (T2V/I2V/V2V), controlled synthetic perturbations with monotonic sensitivity demonstration, cross-estimator robustness analysis (ρ≥0.860), and blinded human study achieving highest correlation (ρ=0.945) among all baselines.

Strong disentanglement from camera motion artifacts: correlation analysis and Figure 6 convincingly show SGC decouples geometric inconsistency from motion dynamics—camera motion explains ≤27% of variance, a critical property missing from competitors.

Interpretable, diagnostic components: rotational/translational variance and depth consistency have clear physical meanings enabling failure mode analysis (Fig. 7b shows component-specific perturbations correctly isolate intended metrics).
Comprehensive methodological documentation: detailed algorithms, PCA weights, hyperparameters, extensive appendix, 10-fold cross-validation confirming weight stability enables reproducibility.
Honest discussion of limitations and thorough ablations demonstrating necessity of each module (Table 2: MOS removal causes >2.5× error increase on RT-1).
weaknesses: Critical dependence on foundational estimators (VGGT, Video Depth Anything) trained on static scenes introduces unquantified domain shift. Paper explicitly acknowledges lacking 'absolute error calibration mechanism' (Appendix A). Depth estimation errors directly corrupt 3D reconstruction and pose estimation—error propagation analysis is absent, limiting confidence in absolute quality judgments.

Scope restricted to static background consistency only—cannot evaluate non-rigid foreground geometry, articulated motion, or dynamic object consistency. This substantially limits utility as a holistic video quality metric, reducing impact to a diagnostic complement rather than primary evaluation tool.

Cascading external dependencies (SegAnyMo for motion segmentation, DELTA for tracking) each introduce failure modes. Appendix D.2 reveals >100% relative error increase under under-segmentation in dynamic scenes (RT-1), while over-segmentation helps static scenes (OpenVid), indicating domain-dependent noise.

PCA-based metric aggregation is objective but lacks principled justification. Translational errors dominate (48.6% weight) vs. rotational (28.4%), but application-dependent importance is not addressed. No sensitivity analysis on how weight distribution affects model rankings or ablation on alternative aggregation schemes.

Limited dataset diversity: all generative videos from single source (GenWorld), and PCA weights derived and evaluated on overlapping distribution. While cross-validation shows generalization within this distribution, out-of-distribution robustness and generalization to other video corpora remain unvalidated.

Methodological novelty is incremental: PnP pose estimation, variance metrics, and depth checking are standard techniques. Primary novelty is application of existing tools (SegAnyMo, VGGT) plus PCA weighting—does not introduce new geometric insights or algorithmic advances.

Human evaluation limited in scale (150 pairs, 7 annotators) with no inter-rater agreement (ICC/Kappa) reported. Instruction to ignore foreground motion is cognitively demanding, and small sample size lacks statistical significance testing or confidence intervals.

Computational cost not analyzed. Pipeline requires VGGT inference, Video Depth Anything, DELTA tracking, SegAnyMo, and PnP solving per frame/region—likely expensive at scale, limiting practical adoption for iterative model development.

No intuitive interpretation of absolute SGC values. Real-world anchors establish lower bounds (0.05–0.06) but gap to generative models (0.08–0.32) lacks guidance on what constitutes 'acceptable' performance. Metric ranking is clear but absolute quality judgments remain ambiguous.

Incomplete failure analysis: no discussion of pathological cases (near-planar scenes, transparent backgrounds, extremely low-motion videos), and unclear how SGC behaves during catastrophic geometric breakdowns when all rigid-world assumptions fail.

strengths: Well-motivated problem: Correctly identifies the gap between fidelity-centric metrics (insensitive to geometry) and consistency metrics (penalize valid motion)
Comprehensive experimental validation: 1,296 videos from 10 generative models and 3 real datasets with extensive ablations, perturbation studies, and robustness analysis across estimators
Physically grounded principle: Core insight that static backgrounds follow a single rigid camera transformation is sound and interpretable
Careful confound analysis: Systematic investigation of camera motion dependency (r≤0.52), MOS quality effects, and estimator robustness
Strong human alignment: Achieves ρ=0.945 correlation with human judgments of 3D background stability
Interpretable component design: Multi-component architecture maps to specific geometric failure modes with clear diagnostic intent
weaknesses: Limited methodological novelty: Straightforward combination of standard techniques (depth clustering, PnP, depth warping); contributes engineering rather than algorithmic innovation unsuitable for top-tier venue

Critical estimator dependency: Entire pipeline relies on VGGT, Video Depth Anything, DELTA, and SegAnyMo trained on real/clean data; catastrophic failure modes on artifact-heavy generative videos not adequately addressed despite acknowledged domain shift risks
Narrow practical scope: Only evaluates static backgrounds while modern generative models produce complex dynamic scenes; limiting utility despite 'complementary tool' framing

Circular validation design: Human study annotators explicitly instructed to ignore everything except what SGC measures, making perfect correlation expected rather than surprising; only 150 pairs from 7 annotators
Depth clustering methodology: 1D clustering can merge non-contiguous surfaces; justification that this improves PnP conditioning is hand-wavy and lacks theoretical grounding

PCA weighting concerns: Fixed weights derived from evaluation dataset itself raises generalizability questions; why maximum variance in this dataset should define geometric inconsistency universally is unexplained

Weak real-world performance: RT-1 correlation with camera dynamics (r=0.44, R²=0.19) contradicts robustness claims; high SGC scores on some real high-motion videos suggest motion/failure conflation persists

Overclaimed results: 'Robustly quantifies inconsistencies' and 'diagnostic precision' overstate confidence given estimator fragility; no evidence that SGC catches novel failure modes beyond what it was designed to detect
Missing practical validation: No demonstration that improving SGC scores improves actual model quality, user perception, or that models trained to optimize SGC produce better videos
Reproducibility gaps: No code release mentioned; hyperparameter choices appear arbitrary; requires coordinating multiple pre-trained models with unclear compatibility on generative content

strengths: Addresses genuine gap in video evaluation: existing metrics either miss geometric failures (FVD) or penalize valid motion (VBench, novel view synthesis metrics)
Physically grounded principle with sound foundation: static background points must adhere to single camera transformation

Exceptionally comprehensive validation: 1,296 videos across 10 generative models, 3 real datasets, synthetic perturbation studies with monotonic response curves, human study (ρ=0.945 vs ρ=0.864-0.400 for baselines)
Successfully disentangles structure from motion: R²<27% on real data showing geometric failures detected independent of camera dynamics
Robust across different estimators: rank correlation ≥0.860 when replacing VGGT with Any4D/Page4D, confirming failures are structural not artifact-induced
Diagnostic precision identifying specific failure modes (geometric warping, perspective failures, object impermanence) missed by existing metrics
Technical rigor: detailed algorithms, standardized normalization, PCA weight stability via 10-fold cross-validation (std≤0.035), fixed weights enabling reproducibility
Effective presentation with clear motivation, informative visualizations, and comprehensive appendix supporting claims
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: depth clustering, PnP estimation, pose variance measurement are established techniques; contribution is primarily in careful combination and validation rather than methodological innovation

Fundamental estimator dependency not fully resolved: paper acknowledges 'SGC currently lacks absolute error calibration mechanism' to disentangle estimator noise from genuine failures, limiting confidence in absolute scores during catastrophic breakdowns

High sensitivity to motion segmentation quality: >100% error increase under under-segmentation in dynamic datasets (Fig. 8); introduces dependency on another noisy component and paradoxical behavior in static scenes

Severely constrained scope by design: only evaluates static backgrounds, explicitly excludes non-rigid object dynamics, limits applicability to action-heavy videos and reduces relevance for comprehensive video quality assessment
Hyperparameter choices lack justification: k_seg=10, S_min=200 appear arbitrary; no sensitivity analysis provided; unclear how robust results are to these thresholds across diverse video types
Comparison methodology concerns: MEt3R uses post-hoc score map masking (not native), VBench uses modified PCA aggregation; these adaptations may not reflect how baselines are typically deployed

Incomplete failure mode analysis: limited discussion of scenarios where SGC produces misleading scores (e.g., systematic depth bias with maintained coherence); edge cases with extreme blur/occlusion not thoroughly explored
Computational cost unaddressed: requires VGGT inference, dense tracking, depth estimation, clustering, multi-region PnP—runtime comparison to FVD/VBench critical for adoption but not quantified
PCA weighting may be model-specific: translational errors dominating PC1 might reflect current failures rather than fundamental importance; generalizability to improved future models unclear
Technical coupling concern: VGGT provides both global camera pose and implicitly drives depth-based partitioning; potential circular dependency not fully addressed
